column5: Niculescu describes the theatre director as a conceptual artist, an architect and a poet, whose job is to build live performances expressing ideas about life. Supports the module 1 framing of the director as an author of the whole production.

The article quotes Stanislavski: there is no stage director who can produce a piece without first finding the directing idea. The quote is taken from Cole and Chinoy (1963), a secondary source. Check the wording against Stanislavski before quoting it.
The article dates Leone de Sommi's treatise on stage direction to 1550. It is usually dated 1556. Check the date before any lesson uses it.

column4: ch-001 director as necessity and messiah
column5: The article's history: realists found the director necessary, and the rebels (Appia, Craig, Meyerhold, Copeau, Piscator, Brecht) cast him as the messiah of a new theatrical synthesis. Usable as a short history of the role, labelled as this article's account.

column4: ch-001 giving objects a theatrical identity
column5: Niculescu argues that puppets, masks and animated objects must get a theatrical identity and a dramaturgical function, and that the director must explore the dramatic potential of each object in its relation to space. Relevant to module 6 on space and designers.
